surfaces.part: hanging cooking pot mouth with light grey contents/interior

answer.evidence: The largest volume is the pot. Its silhouette widens from 5 to 9 px at rows 16-17. Rows 17-19 are a light grey area (L≈147) that reads as the open mouth and contents, with a dark rim on row 16. Below it, rows 20-22 are a dark front body. The pot is therefore seen from slightly above, with a top of about 4 rows and a front of about 3 rows. The tripod legs are thin 1-px poles with no beams, so there are no horizontal faces to judge. The gold hub at rows 25-28 is a small ornament and carries no top-surface requirement. The mouth evidence is borderline because the front face is short.

styleAnswer.evidence: The tripod is a thin, sparse prop, so the per-tile tone count of 0 says nothing for or against it and I judged by eye against the thin references (lamp-crook, bench). It has 22 distinct colours against 14 for both the lamp and the bench, so it is not thinner or flatter than them. Only 24% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 100% for the lamp-crook and 44% for the bench, so most of its outline carries a brown tint rather than a black sticker line. It has 0% near-flat coverage and no large flat fills. The pot, legs and flame show a few tone steps and some variation, though fewer than the richer well and stall references. At this size it would sit acceptably next to the lamp and bench, but I could not make out fine detail, so this is a borderline pass.
